title: Circular Measure Module 3 Lesson 2: Right-Angled Triangles & Sector Partitions custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, angle $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$, leg $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and leg $BC = 6\text{ cm}$. Find the exact value of $\tan(\angle A)$ and the area of the triangle.

A right-angled triangle has an acute angle $\angle A = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$. A circular sector centred at $A$ of radius $6\text{ cm}$ is drawn inside the triangle. Find the exact area of this sector.

A right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ has $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$, $AC = 4\text{ cm}$, $BC = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, and acute angle $\angle A = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. A sector of radius $4\text{ cm}$ centred at $A$ lies inside the triangle. Find the exact area of the triangle that lies outside the sector.

A circular sector of radius $10\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$ has centre $O$ and bounding radii $OA$ and $OB$. A point $P$ on radius $OA$ is such that $PB \perp OA$, forming right triangle $\triangle OPB$. Find the exact area of triangle $\triangle OPB$.

A right-angled triangle has acute angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$. At each acute vertex, a circular sector of radius $4\text{ cm}$ is drawn inside the triangle. Find the exact total area of the two sectors.

In a right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$, $AC = 6\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 8\text{ cm}$, a sector of radius $6\text{ cm}$ centred at $A$ has arc $DE$ meeting $AC$ at $C$ and hypotenuse $AB$ at $E$. Given that $\angle A = 0.927\text{ radians}$, find the perimeter of the region $BCE$ bounded by leg $BC$, segment $EB$, and arc $CE$.
A right triangle has legs $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$. At the vertex adjacent to the $8\text{ cm}$ leg, a sector of radius $4\text{ cm}$ uses the acute angle. Find that angle and sector area.
